Technical Procedure
TitleActivated Sludge.
Procedure
Using Standard Method 14th Edition, 1976, p.96
Introduction

Successful operation of the 
activated sludge process is dependent on laboratory control. Some of the 
laboratory procedures follow. These methods are presented as a group since they 
are interrelated. These groups are Settleability, Sludge Volume Index, Sludge 
Denisty Index, Sludge Age.

This document initiated by Chem. Amany Hussein EL-Kaddah, 
reviewed by Hoda Hasaneen, by quality control Chemist Saad Sadeek Hassanen, and
accepted by eng. Fathy Mahmoud Ragab 
and approved by Eng: Awad M Fatthy Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

This document is accepted by eng. Samir 
Abd El Gilil EDEPC MPIS coordinator, and certified by accountant; Mahmoud 
Mohamed Soliman; EDEPC admin and financial inspection, quality control General 
Director and supervisor of inspection and quality control head sector.
Sampling

Sampling, subsampling, and pipeting two-phase or three-phase samples may 
introduce serious errors. Make and keep such samples homogeneous during 
transfer.Use special handling to insure sample integrity when subsampling. Mix 
small samples with a magnetic stirrer.
Safety Precautions

Store 
sample in resistant-glass or plastic bottles.

Begin analysis as soon as possible because it's 
impractical to be preserved the sample.

If necessary refrigerate sample at 4C up to time of 
analysis to minimize microbiological decomposition of solids.
Bring samples to room temperature before analysis.

 For operation at 103 -105oC and
f) Steam bath.

g) 
Two 1000 ml graduated cylinders with

1- Settleability
Procedure

Run the settleability 
test on activated sludge immediately after the sample taken.

Take the mixed liquor sample at the 
effluent end of the aeration tanks, while the 
return sludge sample should be taken at some points between the final settling 
tank and the point at which the sludge is mixed with the primary effluent.

Determine 
the settleability of mixed liquor and return sludge by allowing 1000 
ml of well-mixed samples of each to settle in 1000 ml graduated cylinders.

Record the 
volume occupied by the sludge to the nearest 5 ml at the end of 30 min. 
Occasionally it is helpful to measure the sludge at various intervals of time, for example every 5,10, 20 and 30 min. The reading at the end of 30 min. generally is used for plant control.

Although the settleability test on return sludge is not used in any of the calculation for 
activated sludge, the result is helpful in determining whather too much or too 
little sludge is being returned from the final settling tank.

The SVI (sludge volume 
index ) of activated sludge is defined as the volume in ml occupied by 1g of 
activated after settling for 30 min. From this definition it may be observed that 
the lower the SVI the better is the settling quality of the aerated mixed liquor. Also, high SVI values indicate poor settling qualities. Sludge with an SVI 
of 100 or less is considered a good settling sludge.
Calculation

The results obtained from 
the suspended matter test ( Water-033-r0 ) and settleability test on the aerated mixed liquor are 
used to obtain SVI.

Sludge age also 
termed solids retention time and also mean cell residence time. It is defined as the 
ratio of the total weight of activated sludge in the plant to the weight of 
activated sludge lost from the system each day. This has proved to be a useful 
tool in controlling some plants. Generally the older the sludge, the higher will 
be the suspended matter and the lower will be the sludge volume index 
 ( SVI ).
